main_issue: Whether Agent D may keep wearing a medical alert bracelet (or cover it) under the new no-visible-accessories rule at tomorrow's area manager visit

A-B.evidence: B says the rule has no medical exceptions (5) and A agrees 'She's right' (6); but B asks why she wasn't told she could cover earrings (8) and A says one rule for everyone (9).

A-C.evidence: C: 'The memo is from head office... Agent A is right' (11); C backs the rejection of the sweatband (26) in line with A's stance.

A-D.evidence: A insists the bracelet must be off or not visible (3, 13, 23, 31); D keeps pressing for cover/sweatband/explaining and finally says 'either my health or my job' (32).

B-C.evidence: B notes the rule has no exceptions (5) and C says exceptions can't be made (11); neither addresses the other directly.

B-D.evidence: B raises D's bracelet (2) but then says the rule has no medical exception (5), and asks whether covering is OK (8), partly echoing D's idea.

C-D.evidence: C says exceptions can't be made (11) and rejects D's sweatband idea: 'A sweatband is an accessory too' (26).
